motion: The town should install an electronic timetable display at the bus shelter
own_claim: Passenger information is useful, but a new display needs a clear maintenance commitment.
own_opening: Passenger information is useful, but a new display needs a clear maintenance commitment.
chunks: I propose one timetable display at the central bus shelter, operating from seven in the morning until seven in the evening.
The printed timetable would remain alongside it. The display would show scheduled departures, not live vehicle positions.
The installation grant is available, but responsibility for paying future electricity and repairs has not been assigned.
checks: Recognizes one display at the central shelter with seven-to-seven operating hours
Acknowledges that the printed timetable remains and does not describe the proposal as providing live vehicle tracking
Engages the unassigned ongoing electricity or repair responsibility without treating the installation grant as absent or all maintenance as already funded

motion: The college should let student clubs reserve classrooms in the evening
own_claim: Evening classroom reservations could give student clubs a useful place to meet.
own_opening: Evening classroom reservations could give student clubs a useful place to meet.
chunks: I oppose unrestricted evening access, but would permit a four-week trial on Tuesdays from six until eight in two ground-floor classrooms.
A named staff contact must be on duty. If that contact is unavailable, the rooms stay closed; clubs would not be charged a room fee.
Who funds the staff contact is still undecided. I am not claiming that student clubs have already damaged any room.
checks: Recognizes that the opponent permits a four-week Tuesday six-to-eight trial in two ground-floor rooms, rather than opposing all access
Acknowledges the named staff contact requirement and closure fallback rather than accusing the opponent of allowing unsupervised access
Engages the unresolved staff funding without inventing prior damage or a proposed room fee

motion: The residents association should hold a seed exchange
own_claim: A seed exchange needs a manageable scope and someone responsible for unused stock.
own_opening: A seed exchange needs a manageable scope and someone responsible for unused stock.
chunks: The proposal is one Sunday morning exchange of unopened commercial herb-seed packets at the association office.
Participation is free, and packets without a printed expiry date would not be accepted. This proposal includes no seedlings or garden chemicals.
A volunteer has offered to check the labels. Storage and disposal of packets left at the end still need an agreed plan.
checks: Recognizes one Sunday morning exchange restricted to unopened commercial herb-seed packets
Acknowledges free participation and the printed-expiry requirement without treating seedlings or chemicals as included
Engages the unresolved leftover-stock plan without claiming no label checker has been offered or asserting that these packets are known to be unsafe

motion: The department should make lecture audio available to enrolled students
own_claim: Lecture audio could help enrolled students revisit difficult material while respecting consent.
own_opening: Lecture audio could help enrolled students revisit difficult material while respecting consent.

prior_history.content: I oppose all lecture recording because lecturers and students should control their spoken contributions.
Could a limited class-only recording with consent protect that control while allowing students to revisit explanations?

chunks: I withdraw my blanket objection. I would allow lecturer-approved audio in the enrolled class portal for seven days after each lecture.
Recording would pause during student questions, and lecturers could decline without having to give a reason.
No public uploads are included. The unresolved issue is who checks consent and removes files when the seven days expire.
Revisiting an explanation may be useful; I have no evidence that recording necessarily reduces attendance.
checks: Recognizes the replacement position permits lecturer-approved class-portal audio for seven days, rather than maintaining a blanket ban
Acknowledges pausing during student questions and the lecturer right to decline, and does not treat public uploads as allowed
Engages consent administration or timely deletion without attributing an established attendance decline to the opponent

motion: The council should permit a refreshments stall beside the river path
own_claim: Any riverside trading needs to preserve path access and provide a practical waste plan.
own_opening: Any riverside trading needs to preserve path access and provide a practical waste plan.

prior_history.content: A permanent riverside kiosk could sell food and drinks throughout the week.
A permanent structure could obstruct the path. Who would manage food preparation and waste?
I accept that the permanent structure should not proceed while these questions remain open.
Refreshments for walkers could still be considered separately from a permanent building.

chunks: The earlier permanent kiosk is withdrawn. I now propose a movable drinks-only stall on two Saturday afternoons, with no cooking or groundworks.
The stall must leave a two-metre clear path and will not operate during a flood warning.
The operator accepts taking all waste away after each afternoon. The council has not yet assigned someone to verify that cleanup.
The trial could offer refreshments to walkers, but I am making no claim about increased tourism revenue.
checks: Recognizes a movable drinks-only stall for two Saturday afternoons, replacing the permanent kiosk and excluding cooking or groundworks
Acknowledges the two-metre clear path and no-operation flood-warning condition
Engages cleanup verification without claiming waste removal was refused or inventing tourism revenue

motion: The association should allow members to vote remotely
own_claim: Remote voting could include members unable to attend, provided the voting rules remain clear.
own_opening: Remote voting could include members unable to attend, provided the voting rules remain clear.

prior_history.content: I oppose allowing any remote vote because the association needs confidence in voter identity.
Members who cannot attend still have a stake in the election. Could we separate identity checking from recording the vote?

chunks: My earlier opposition to all remote votes is withdrawn. For the next committee election only, I would permit remote voting by existing members whose membership is verified before voting.
Each member gets one ballot, whether voting at the meeting or remotely; there is no extra remote-voting fee.
Verification must not expose how a member votes. The specific method for separating identity checks from secret ballots is still undecided.
I accept that this could help members who cannot attend. I have not established that remote voting has caused fraud in this association.
checks: Recognizes permission for verified existing members to vote remotely in the next committee election, rather than continued opposition to all remote votes
Acknowledges one ballot per member across both channels and the requirement to preserve ballot secrecy
Engages the undecided identity/secrecy method without inventing a remote-voting fee or established association fraud

motion: The library should provide temporary storage lockers
own_claim: Lockers need an accessible opening process and a clear policy for keys and left-behind items.
own_opening: Lockers need an accessible opening process and a clear policy for keys and left-behind items.

prior_history.content: Library lockers could give visitors somewhere to leave bags while using the reading rooms.
How would visitors who cannot operate the locks gain access, and would they have to leave a large deposit?
I accept staff assistance on request for visitors unable to operate a lock. That will be a condition of any trial.
That addresses lock operation. Replacement costs and the end-of-day handling of belongings still need a plan.

chunks: The current proposal is six lockers during library opening hours for a five-week trial, with no overnight storage.
The assistance arrangement we already agreed remains part of the proposal. Use of a locker would be free, with no cash key deposit.
Users must empty lockers by closing time. Responsibility for lost-key replacement costs is still undecided.
I accept publishing an unclaimed-item procedure before the trial begins, but no reduction in theft has been measured.
checks: Recognizes six lockers for five weeks, usable only during library opening hours without overnight storage
Acknowledges staff assistance on request for users unable to operate a lock, and the free no-cash-deposit terms
Engages lost-key replacement responsibility without claiming the unclaimed-item procedure was refused or inventing measured theft reductions

motion: The tenants association should offer a remote way to attend its monthly meetings
own_claim: Remote attendance could let tenants participate when they cannot get to the meeting room.
own_opening: Remote attendance could let tenants participate when they cannot get to the meeting room.

prior_history.content: I am concerned that a remote connection could disrupt speaking turns and compromise privacy.
Would a text channel for requesting a speaking turn, with no recording of the meeting, address those concerns?
I accept the text request channel and a rule that the meeting will not be recorded. A person still needs to monitor that channel.
The remaining question is who will monitor remote participation alongside the chair.

chunks: I would permit an optional remote audio connection for the next three monthly meetings, with the in-person meeting continuing as usual.
The participation and privacy arrangements already agreed remain in force. No participant would be required to switch on a camera.
Someone must monitor remote requests to speak, but the volunteer rota for that task is not yet filled.
I accept publishing connection instructions a week before each meeting. I have no evidence that remote attendees are less committed than those in the room.
checks: Recognizes the opponent permits optional remote audio at the next three monthly meetings while retaining in-person attendance
Acknowledges the previously accepted text channel for requests to speak and the no-recording rule, without demanding mandatory cameras
Engages the unfilled remote-participation rota without treating advance connection instructions as refused or inventing lower attendee commitment

motion: The council should translate its neighborhood notices
own_claim: Translated notices need an explicit review process and sustainable publication costs.
own_opening: Translated notices need an explicit review process and sustainable publication costs.

prior_history.content: Translated notices could make council instructions accessible to more residents.
How would the council catch a translation that reverses an instruction or gives the wrong collection date?
I accept having a named fluent reviewer check each translated notice before publication. Machine output alone would not be sufficient.
That establishes a review requirement, but the appointment and payment of reviewers still need a plan.

chunks: The immediate proposal covers four monthly waste-collection notices in two additional languages. Other council documents are outside this trial.
The original English notice remains available, and all versions would be free. The review arrangement we already agreed still applies.
Translations could make instructions easier to access, but I have no measured effect on recycling rates.
Funding for the named reviewers remains unassigned. The notices should not be issued in translation before those reviewers are appointed.
checks: Recognizes four monthly waste-collection notices in two additional languages, rather than translation of all council documents
Acknowledges a named fluent reviewer checking each translated notice before publication, with the original English retained
Engages reviewer appointment or funding as a prepublication issue without treating free access as a fee or inventing recycling improvements

motion: The neighborhood center should create a food-sharing hub
own_claim: A food-sharing hub needs clear handling responsibilities and a workable operating budget.
own_opening: A food-sharing hub needs clear handling responsibilities and a workable operating budget.

prior_history.content: The center could host a pantry, a community fridge, a cooked-food event and a recipe exchange.
These involve different handling tasks. Which services would actually start, and who would run them?
A delivery round, a growers table and a cooking lesson are other possible uses. I accept that current funding cannot cover every option.
The initial request needs a precise scope. Each actual session also needs cleaning and supervision.

chunks: The immediate request is two Saturday collection sessions for sealed shelf-stable food packets. Refrigeration and cooked meals are future options, not part of this request.
Packets must be within their printed expiry date. Collection is free, and no household income documents are required.
I accept keeping cleaning records after each session and publishing a summary at the end of the trial.
A named coordinator must supervise each session. We have not identified who will pay that coordinator.
The hub may provide useful supplies to some households; it does not establish a measured reduction in household hunger.
checks: Recognizes two Saturday sessions limited to sealed shelf-stable packets, excluding immediate refrigeration or cooked meals
Acknowledges the expiry-date check and free collection without income documentation
Engages the coordinator funding or supervision without claiming cleaning is deferred until the trial ends or inventing measured hunger reductions

motion: The school should publish a digital newsletter for families
own_claim: A digital newsletter could make school information easier for families to obtain.
own_opening: A digital newsletter could make school information easier for families to obtain.

prior_history.content: A school communication platform could include a newsletter, student photos, polls, public comments and advertising. I object to treating all those features as one harmless package.
Could we evaluate a simple newsletter separately from photos, polls or public comments?
A calendar, event reminders and club listings are also possible. No item should publish a student home address or private contact details.
Agreed on protecting private details. We still need to decide the initial scope and who checks each issue.

chunks: I would allow a text-only newsletter for two issues over one month. Student photographs, public comments and advertising would not be included.
Families could choose a printed copy at no charge instead. They would not have to install an app or create an online account.
A named editor must check items before release. The privacy rules we discussed remain necessary, but I am not claiming a privacy incident has already occurred.
The editor workload and funding are unsettled. Easier access to dates and notices is a possible benefit even though no improvement in academic results is established.
checks: Recognizes the opponent allows a text-only two-issue one-month trial, excluding photographs, public comments and advertising
Acknowledges the free printed alternative without requiring an app or account
Engages editor workload or funding while acknowledging possible access benefits, without inventing an existing privacy breach or academic gains

motion: The school should allow community groups to use its playing field
own_claim: Community field access could provide useful recreation while preserving school priority.
own_opening: Community field access could provide useful recreation while preserving school priority.

prior_history.content: Possible uses include evening football, weekend tournaments, walking groups and fitness classes. I oppose opening the field without distinguishing these activities.
A limited walking session could be considered independently of tournaments and evening floodlights.
A running circuit, a charity fair and a holiday camp are other suggestions. School activities must keep priority over community use.
Agreed on school priority. Who would decide whether the surface can support the specific activity on the day?

chunks: My objection is to unrestricted access. I would permit prebooked adult walking groups on three Wednesday afternoons from four to six.
School activities keep priority, no floodlights would be used, and any booking is canceled if the groundkeeper closes the field because of surface conditions.
There would be no booking fee during this trial. I accept that a sign-in contact would be published before reservations open.
Who pays for extra ground inspections is still undecided. A walking opportunity is a possible benefit, not proof that injuries or maintenance costs will fall.
checks: Recognizes permission for prebooked adult walking groups on three Wednesdays from four to six, rather than opposition to every community use
Acknowledges school priority, no floodlights and groundkeeper closure overriding a booking
Engages the inspection funding without inventing a booking fee, refused sign-in disclosure or proven injury/maintenance savings
